1. Hydrotherapy pool shell and balance tank, including the pool overflow gutters, tiled steps, underwater light recesses and movement joints. Continue the membrane around the balance tank access neck and seal each return pipe where it passes through the tank wall;
2. Elderly wing assisted bathing rooms, including wheelchair shower bays, hoist bases, floor drain collars and doorway thresholds. Turn the waterproofing up behind the wall lining and seal the junctions with sanitary fittings and the shower seat brackets;
3. Youth wing laundry and cleaning stores, including washing machine plinths, mop sink upstands and pipe sleeves. Provide a continuous membrane beneath removable service trays and beneath every machine base, with accessible seals around the trapped drain outlets;
4. Therapy garden water feature and pump pit, including basin corners, cable entry sleeves and the overflow channel. Extend the waterproofing beneath the feature finishes and around the pump pit cover frame, protecting it where maintenance ladders bear on the surface;
5. Basement kitchen cold room floors and service trenches, including trench intersections, drain sumps and door frame bases;
 Continue the waterproofing below the insulated wall panels, seal every access cover seating and provide compatible returns around the refrigerant pipe openings;
6. Staff accommodation bathroom floors and wet wall junctions, including shower kerbs, basin waste penetrations and recessed cupboards. Carry the membrane beneath the bath supports and across every threshold before laying the floor finishes;
7. Eastern retaining wall tanking and adjacent stairwell drainage recess, including construction joints, wall to footing junctions and service ducts. Protect the membrane before backfilling and leave inspection access at each drainage collection point;
8. Covered entrance planters and rainwater collection channels, including irrigation sleeves and emergency overflow outlets;
 Return the waterproofing over the planter rims and seal each junction with the entrance paving, keeping the root protection layers clear of the channel inspection covers;
9. Emergency generator room fuel containment bund and washdown apron, including the bund corners, cable duct crossings and discharge collection sump. Provide continuous waterproofing beneath equipment pads and seal the movement joint between the bund and the apron.

Coordination request for the youth and elderly centre

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R101 Date 2026-08-03 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

Dear project team, we are preparing the NTT, SCT and SCC for the proposed youth and elderly centre. Please provide the adopted scope, pricing documents, component responsibilities, warranty coverage and arrangements for inspecting the tender information.

This request is a list of questions, not confirmation of any answer. Please use the replies for this project. Where no business decision has been made, refer the question to the reviewer rather than filling it from a standard form.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

DRAFTING EXTRACTION PROTOCOL. Return only a JSON array of supported items {key,value,sourceQuote,reason,confidence}. Use native JSON values: object, array, boolean, number, string or null, according to the single catalogue below. Example contract value: {"number":"C-2026/10","title":"Works A"}. A supported partial contract may omit its missing sibling. Example Bill value: [{"number":"1","description":"Exact formal description"}]. Never invent missing identifiers or descriptions. Requests asking for missing information, questions and explicitly pending classifications are not answers. Actual project instructions or decisions can support editable suggestions; later UI adoption is separate. A reference to another source does not supply that source's missing details. Return no guessed values or empty copies of the catalogue. If the source expressly leaves an input pending, not supplied or blank, return that key with value null, its explanation and one exact contiguous unresolved-source quote. Only inputs unmentioned in this part may be omitted. false is an explicit No and [] an explicitly justified empty list. Collections have three states: source-confirmed absence is []; pending, missing information or insufficient facts are null; explicitly provided applicable items are a concrete list. [] requires an exact quote and complete original context establishing absence for this field and scope. A failed search is not absence. Examples: 'No additional tender requirements apply to this project.' -> value []; 'Additional tender requirements remain pending.' or 'No requirement can be established from the available facts.' -> value null; 'Provide a signed plan with the tender.' -> value [{"text":"Provide a signed plan with the tender."}]. Only text inside correspondence-part establishes values; templates, filenames, metadata and catalogue labels are not evidence. Quotes must be contiguous source passages, copied exactly including punctuation. Use a short passage for scalar values; for a collection or numbered list, quote the complete defining list/table and its governing heading. Return every supplied applicable item in original order and retain its numbering and wording, including the final catch-all item. Never return only the prefix or tail of one complete source list. Confidence must be between 0 and 1. Preserve formal English names. Type/purpose classifications are separate from literal Bill descriptions. Bill type, purpose, trade and issue placement are optional: omit unknown cells. Each classification requires explicit evidence for that exact row; a schedule heading or the name Preliminaries does not classify every Bill. Bill rows may put pricing type before or after the number/description. Use the actual header to bind columns. BQ1 and SOR1 are different identities. A description containing '(All Provisional)' is a formal name, not evidence about every BQ quantity. Keep numeric roles separate: a repayment period in months is not its first payment-certificate number. English number words and ordinals denote the same numbers. An input whose catalogue condition is false is not applicable: return null, never false as a substitute. Known contractorLegalForm makes the two fallback clause-adoption inputs unnecessary; the business rules derive clause treatment from the known form. L10Pro pricing preparation is independent of paper/DVD return. NSC/BSSSC arrangement is independent of trade scope. otherTenderingArrangement is only an explicitly adopted alternative to the two-envelope tender procedure or replacement SCT5 wording. Hardcopy plus DVD-ROM submission under the existing two-envelope procedure is return media, not an alternative tender procedure; do not map it to this input. A selected-trades quote must explicitly cover every selected trade. Cite a contiguous selected-trade table or the sentence defining the list, not only the NSC/BSSSC arrangement. Do not select No/excluded rows or duplicate combined Fire services and water pump or Lift and escalator with their shorter options. Combined-foundation classification and >=39-month threshold are separate inputs; a baseline/ceiling does not establish the exact accepted period. Derived results and targetOverrides are excluded. Suggestions are never automatic adoption.

Contract identity and initial foundation coordination

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R102 Date 2026-08-04 Meeting minutes

Attendees: Fictional Project Architect, Structural Engineer, Procurement Officer and Quantity Surveyor. Recorder: Fictional Quantity Surveyor.

We confirmed Contract No. 20260983, Construction of Youth and Elderly Centre at Sha Tin Area 34. The centre includes a domestic residential accommodation block for resident staff. All buildings are in Sha Tin; there are no works in Tin Shui Wai.

Foundation works and building works are included in this combined contract. The Contractor designs and constructs the driven piling for the centre. The Architect designs the pile caps and the shallow footings, which the Contractor constructs.

This initial coordination covers piling, pilecaps and footings only. It is not a complete schedule of components, and the actual work limits will be supplied in the detailed responsibility reply. The three initial entries are:
Component | Contractor designs | Contractor executes
piling | Yes | Yes
pilecaps | No | Yes
footings | No | Yes

Complete component responsibilities and tender submissions

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R107 Date 2026-08-11 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

This is the complete component responsibility schedule, including the boundary retaining walls omitted from the initial coordination. It supplies the work limits for the earlier three entries and does not change their design or execution assignments.
Component | Actual work scope | Contractor executes | Contractor designs
piling | Driven steel piles for the youth wing | Yes | Yes
pilecaps | Architect designed pile caps for the youth wing | Yes | No
footings | Shallow footings for the elderly wing and covered entrance | Yes | No
other | Architect designed retaining walls along the eastern boundary | Yes | No

The shallow footings serve the elderly wing building and the covered entrance, which is a major external structure.

The Contractor must submit its proposed piling foundation design with the Tender. The final foundation design is not established at tender acceptance; it remains subject to subsequent checking and approval.

RSE endorsed submissions are not required for this project. The additional tender submissions are:
Submit an accessible pedestrian diversion plan with the Tender.
Submit a vibration monitoring proposal for the neighbouring care home with the Tender.

The question whether a design related quotation must be obtained before a Variation is instructed remains open. This reply records neither adoption nor rejection of that optional requirement.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

No Works Subject to Excision are specified. Site formation works are excluded because the site is already formed. An Excavation Permit is not required: this contract has no excavation in a public road.

Subsidised Sale Flats production is included in the domestic block. Both exhibition flats and show flats are required.

CON8 volumetric precast components are used in the domestic residential accommodation block. The project is in Sha Tin rather than Tin Shui Wai.

Submit PSE endorsed connection details for the domestic CON8 modules.

The Tender is based on precast concrete facades. Precast facades are required and are permitted under APE2.A410.

The WTO Government Procurement Agreement applies to this fictional tender.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

Adopted construction scope and precast requirements

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R109 Date 2026-08-13 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

No Works Subject to Excision are specified. Site formation works are excluded because the site is already formed. An Excavation Permit is not required: this contract has no excavation in a public road.

Subsidised Sale Flats production is included in the domestic block. Both exhibition flats and show flats are required.

CON8 volumetric precast components are used in the domestic residential accommodation block. The project is in Sha Tin rather than Tin Shui Wai.

The PSE submission requirements for those domestic CON8 components are:
Submit PSE endorsed connection details for the domestic CON8 modules.
Submit PSE endorsed lifting and temporary stability calculations for the domestic CON8 modules.

The Tender is based on precast concrete facades. Precast facades are required and are permitted under APE2.A410.

The WTO Government Procurement Agreement applies to this fictional tender.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor
</correspondence-part>

Architect appointment and inspection arrangements

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R112 Date 2026-08-18 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

For SCT7, the Project Architect post is Chief Architect Welfare Buildings. Address the appointed officer as Ms. Her name is Sylvia P. Y. CHAN.

The Project Architect telephone number has not been confirmed. Use the fictional coordination mailbox appointments@consense-scenario.invalid for enquiries while the telephone detail is pending.

The Specification Library can be inspected on floor 7, Block E, Fictional Tender Information Office, 66 Study Road, Sha Tin.

The drawings can be inspected on floor 2, Block F, Fictional Tender Information Office, 66 Study Road, Sha Tin.

Site inspections may start on 16 September 2026. The end date is awaiting confirmation and must not be inferred from the start date or the length of the contract.

Adopt these site visit restrictions:
Book the visit by email at least seven working days in advance.
A visit may include no more than four people, all wearing safety helmets and high visibility vests.
Visitors must be accompanied by the site escort and must not enter the tree protection areas.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

decisions.rawValue: 1. Hydrotherapy pool shell and balance tank, including the pool overflow gutters, tiled steps, underwater light recesses and movement joints. Continue the membrane around the balance tank access neck and seal each return pipe where it passes through the tank wall; 2. Elderly wing assisted bathing rooms, including wheelchair shower bays, hoist bases, floor drain collars and doorway thresholds. Turn the waterproofing up behind the wall lining and seal the junctions with sanitary fittings and the shower seat brackets; 3. Youth wing laundry and cleaning stores, including washing machine plinths, mop sink upstands and pipe sleeves. Provide a continuous membrane beneath removable service trays and beneath every machine base, with accessible seals around the trapped drain outlets; 4. Therapy garden water feature and pump pit, including basin corners, cable entry sleeves and the overflow channel. Extend the waterproofing beneath the feature finishes and around the pump pit cover frame, protecting it where maintenance ladders bear on the surface; 5. Basement kitchen cold room floors and service trenches, including trench intersections, drain sumps and door frame bases; Continue the waterproofing below the insulated wall panels, seal every access cover seating and provide compatible returns around the refrigerant pipe openings; 6. Staff accommodation bathroom floors and wet wall junctions, including shower kerbs, basin waste penetrations and recessed cupboards. Carry the membrane beneath the bath supports and across every threshold before laying the floor finishes; 7. Eastern retaining wall tanking and adjacent stairwell drainage recess, including construction joints, wall to footing junctions and service ducts. Protect the membrane before backfilling and leave inspection access at each drainage collection point; 8. Covered entrance planters and rainwater collection channels, including irrigation sleeves and emergency overflow outlets; Return the waterproofing over the planter rims and seal each junction with the entrance paving, keeping the root protection layers clear of the channel inspection covers; 9. Emergency generator room fuel containment bund and washdown apron, including the bund corners, cable duct crossings and discharge collection sump. Provide continuous waterproofing beneath equipment pads and seal the movement joint between the bund and the apron.

Submit a vibration monitoring proposal for the neighbouring care home with the Tender.

The question whether a design related quotation must be obtained before a Variation is instructed remains open. This reply records neither adoption nor rejection of that optional requirement.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor
